key_insight: BaTiO₃/nickelate superlattices show qualitatively similar interfacial polar-discontinuity responses whether the nickelate is insulating or metallic, despite metallic screening charges.
engineering_relevance: These findings inform electrostatic modeling of nickelate/ferroelectric interfaces, rather than directly demonstrating AI methods or solar-cell performance.
method: Use first-principles calculations for BaTiO₃/SmNiO₃ and BaTiO₃/BiNiO₃ superlattices.
Compare insulating and metallic nickelate phases.
Analyze structural changes, density of states, and charge-disproportionation patterns.
evidence_signal: The calculations identify polar-discontinuity signatures and partial screening through altered BiNiO₃ charge disproportionation, with qualitatively similar interfacial responses in metallic counterparts.
watch_item: The formal-charge polar-discontinuity picture has practical limits for interpreting and quantifying screening at metallic nickelate/ferroelectric interfaces.
paper_title: The polar discontinuity picture in nickelate superlattices: comparison of the insulating and metallic phases
